notes: Shopify storefront (serax.com). Checked main nav, mega-menu, footer, all /pages links, and full sitemap.xml -> sitemap_collections_1/2.xml (2500+250 loc entries, deduped with the site's /collections.json paged listing, 3137 unique collections total): no canonical 'Bestsellers'/'Best Sellers'/'Top Sellers'/'Popular'/'Customer Favorites' nav item or collection handle exists (direct probes of /collections/bestsellers, /best-sellers, /popular, /customer-favorites all 404). Used the site's own /search/suggest.json endpoint (resources[type]=collection) for 'bestsellers'/'best sellers' and it returned exactly 2 published, non-hidden collections: bestsellers-jan-25 (site title 'Bestsellers feb 25', published 2025-02-21) and bestsellers-apr-25 (site title 'Bestsellers apr 25', published 2025-05-08). Both opened and confirmed as real small PLPs (product grid, not editorial) via exhaustive /collections/<handle>/products.json pagination: 9 unique product IDs each, only 2 of the 9 IDs shared between the two (mostly distinct sets), so kept as two separate rows rather than merged. Neither is linked from main nav/mega-menu/footer -- both are only reachable by direct URL or via site search, and both are dated, month-stamped snapshot names with no newer instalment found (latest is Apr 2025, >1 year stale as of this pass, 2026-09-08) and no ongoing 'Bestsellers' program page like the one found for Clearance (see cl162.json 'Archive Sale' hub). Flagged both for manual review: cannot confirm the site currently treats these as an active, ongoing bestsellers merchandising surface versus a one-off past marketing artifact that was never taken down. No local-language (NL/FR) equivalent search terms (meest verkocht, meilleures ventes) returned anything additional -- collection handles are shared across locales on this storefront, only titles are translated, so the English-term sweep already covers the full collection set.
